0.value:
Corrects the Shadow arm sensors. First, if it is given one, the take's T-pose turn (elbow_turn measures it): how far each elbow was turned when the suit was calibrated. Then four corrections per arm, each an angle worked out afresh every frame:

  roll   the upper arm turned about its own bone
  yaw    the upper arm turned about vertical
  fyaw   the forearm turned about vertical
  hang   the whole arm turned sideways about the chest's forward axis, coming in as
         the arm drops from 25 to 55 degrees below level (judged where
         the correction puts the arm, so the error can't hide an arm)

Each angle is a weighted sum of numbers that say how the sensor sits. Six are the world's two horizontal axes, seen from inside the sensor: the shape a magnetization (hard-iron) error takes, which unlike a heading stays defined when the arm hangs straight down. The roll also uses two about the body: how high the arm is, and how far the elbow is bent past 62 degrees (the middle of elbow_turn's band, where the turn sets the roll) - for a strap, cable or muscle that pulls the sensor round as the arm moves. The hang is one number per arm: lowered arms that sit to one side together (a good T-pose, then an asymmetric hang) is a common Shadow error. The corrected upper arm and forearm are written back into the shoulder, elbow and wrist; the hand keeps where it was in the world, under 'hang' too.

The 42 weights are meant to be learned: t.param holds them and t.optimize tunes them to keep the elbows on their hinges (elbow_hinge) and the lowered arms centred (hang_symmetry). Give it one pose and it corrects
that pose; give it a whole take and it corrects every frame at once, keeping the trail for t.optimize.

SYNTAX:
shadow_mag_correct

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

pose in:
Shadow quaternions, scalar first: one pose (37 or 20 joints, 4 each) or a take (frames, joints, 4). Numpy in gives numpy out; a tensor stays a tensor.

weights:
42 numbers, in radians, 21 per arm, left arm then right: roll (6 field numbers, then arm height and elbow bend), yaw (6), fyaw (6), hang (1; positive moves a hanging arm toward the dancer's left). A shorter list fills the rest with 0; the older 40- and 36-number layouts are still accepted. New weights
re-correct the pose already held, so a paused body follows the learning.

turn:
Two numbers in degrees, left then right: the take's T-pose turn, from elbow_turn. It is undone before the learned corrections. Also re-corrects the held pose.

fixed bank (float box, also an inlet):
Degrees, as hang_symmetry's shift reads it (+ toward the dancer's left). Used only when 'hang from' is 'fixed bank': both arms then undo this bank instead of taking the hang from the weights. Also re-corrects the held pose.

correct (checkbox, also an inlet):
Off passes the pose through untouched - for comparing.

amount (float box, also an inlet):
Scales the correction, turn included: 0 none, 1 all of it.

roll, yaw, fyaw, hang:
Options, under the node: switch each correction on or off.

turn fade:
An option, in degrees of elbow bend (0 by default). With the arm straight nothing shows the turn; above 0 the turn comes in smoothly from none with the arm straight to all of it at this bend. 0 undoes all of it everywhere.

hang from:
An option: 'weights' (the default) learns the hang with the rest; 'fixed bank' takes it from the 'fixed bank' inlet instead. Use 'fixed bank' for takes recorded with Shadow's fusion before 2025-12-18, where a session's bank is steady: measure it once over all of the session's takes (np.robust_mean of hang_symmetry's shift per take, or of the banks of every arms-down frame) and apply that one number to every take of the session. The other corrections can still be learned alongside; the hang weights are then ignored.

OUTPUTS:

pose out:
The corrected pose or take, in the layout it came in.

READING THE DEMO:
At rest every sensor is level, so the first feature is 1, and 0.35 - the first of the 42 weights, the rest 0 - turns the left upper arm 0.35 radians (20 degrees) about its bone. Click the button: the left_shoulder row of the angles shows the roll, and the left_elbow row the opposite turn, so the forearm stays where it was in the world.

RELATED:
elbow_hinge and hang_symmetry measure the errors the weights are learned against;
t.param and t.optimize learn them. elbow_turn measures the turn. shadow_arm_correct is the hand-dialled arm fix; mag_yaw_correct sets constant yaw offsets. The full learning setup on a real take is examples/shadow_mag_learning.json.
